Definition: from G3784; indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty:--debt, due.
BiblicalUsage: A debt is what is owed, and Paul uses the word twice in very different places: husbands and wives owe one another due benevolence in marriage, and the unforgiving servant in the parable was forgiven all his debt by his lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe debt cuts both ways in Scripture: what I owe others I must pay gladly, and what I owe God I could never pay, which is why His forgiveness is everything.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
